To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an antibody that exhibits O-glycan-independent binding to NT-proBNP.

we have developed an antibody that recognizes the Gly63–K68 epitope of Nt-proBNP with O-glycosylated-independent binding, and that this antibody can be used for the development of a new NT-proBNP immunoassay with high sensitivity.

the epitope of an antibody that reacts with the N-terminal fragment of the prohormone of brain natriurectic peptide (NT-pro-BNP) was defined as Gly 63 – Lys 68 and that the antibody binds to the deglycosylatied form of NT-pro-BNP with a similar affinity to that observed with the native form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the development of an antibody that exhibits a glycosylation-independent reaction.
the development of a glycosylation-independent assay system for NT-proBNP.
the development of a new antibody that exhibits glycan-independent binding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epitope of the antibody is Gly63–Lye68 of NT-pro-BNP, and the O-glycosylated region does not interfere with the antibody binding.
the Gly63–Kys68 epitope is located within the region of NT-proBNPs that is not O-glycosylated.
an antibody reactive with the Gly63–K68 of NT-proBPNP exhibits glycosylation independent binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gly63–Gly68 region is the most tolerant of O-glycosylated NT-proBNP.
we succeeded in the development of an antibody that can be used to detect NT-proBNP with a high affinity and without interference of glycosylation.
the epitope of the antibody is located in a region of NT-proBNPt hat is not affected by glycosylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Gly63–Gly64 bond of NT-proBNN is important for the binding of the antibody, which is the same as the case for the binding of a monoclonal antibody to the N-terminal region of the BNP precursor peptide.
an antibody reactive with an epitope located in the middle of a glycosylated protein can exhibit glycosylation-independent affinity.
the Gly63–Kys68 epitope is not affected by O-glycosylated modifications.
